entries.title: How to found a town
q: how do i start a town
how do i found a village
how do i create a town
how do i make my own town
how do i start a village of my own
how do i make a city
can i build my own village
entries.answer: Right-click your Founding Kit (or press U → Start a village) and the founding screen opens: pick where, how big, a name and a look, then Confirm and found. The ground is levelled and the founders walk in and build the town themselves.
entries.notown: You haven't founded a town yet — here's how.
steps: Right-click the Founding Kit (new players get one), or press U and choose Start a village.
Where: 'Here' or one of up to three better spots near you, each scored out of 100 with its reason. Look at it shows the outline on the real ground.
How big: Hamlet (8), Village (25), Town (70), City (250), or any number on the slider.
Name it (or press Another for a new suggestion) and pick its look.
Tick Take me there if you want to be carried to it, then press Confirm and found.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Ask → Favours → Start a village of my own
tips: Founding uses up a Founding Kit, else a Village Folk Spawner, else a Village Charter (free in creative).
Start with a Village of about 25: big enough for trades and growth, light on the server.
warn: A server can limit who may found (everyone, citizens or operators) and how many towns each player may found (3 by default).

entries.title: Choosing where to found
q: where should i found my town
how do i pick a spot for my town
what do the site scores mean
how is the town site chosen
entries.answer: The founding screen offers 'Here' and up to three better spots within about 160 blocks, each scored out of 100 with its reason (e.g. 'flat meadow by a river, oak wood 20 blocks'). Flat ground counts most; then dry ground, water and wood nearby, solid ground (no caves), above the sea and clear of other towns.
steps: On the Where step, read each spot's score and reason; the map shows them (H is here, 1-3 the others, red squares are towns).
Press Look at it: the screen hides and the outline shows on the ground (gold the square, green the first ring of lots and street, white the ground to be levelled).
Walk round it, then press U to come back to the screen.
Pick the best and go on to How big.
controls: Founding screen → Where → Look at it
tips: Spots too near another town, in the sea or mostly water aren't offered.
A river or lake beside the square is fine: the square ends in a quay rather than being cut into the water.

entries.title: How big to make a town
q: how many folk should i start with
how big should my town be
what size village should i make
what does the founding slider do
entries.answer: Pick a Hamlet of 8, a Village of 25, a Town of 70, a City of 250, or any number from 2 up to the server's limit (500 at most). The screen says what that means: the ground levelled, the trades they'll take, the homes they'll want, and the cost to the server.
steps: Choose a preset or drag the slider.
Read 'What that means': it turns amber from about a hundred folk and red from three hundred.
Confirm when happy.
tips: A small town grows by itself: two fed folk in work raise children while there's room and food put by.
Bigger parties bring more founding stores and bedding.
warn: Hundreds of folk are heavy for a server: every one is a ticking creature.

entries.title: Naming a town and choosing its look
q: how do i name my town
what building style will my town have
pick a theme for my village
entries.answer: On the founding screen's How big step, the name is suggested for you: press Another for a new one, or type your own. Pick the look from the themes on offer. The town then builds in its land's own woods and stone in that style.
steps: Type a name, or press Another.
Choose a look from the list.
Confirm and found.
tips: A town's walls are of the wood its woods grow and its footings of the land's own stone, so each town reads differently.
The look grows with the ages: stone walls in the Stone Age, slate roofs in the Iron Age, copper on the great roofs in the Diamond Age.

entries.title: Take me there
q: what does take me there do
how do i get to my new village
will i be teleported to the town
entries.answer: Ticked on the founding screen, Take me there carries you to the edge of the new town's ground when you confirm, falling softly, if the server allows it and the spot is within reach (256 blocks by default). Otherwise you walk.

entries.title: What happens after you found
q: what happens after i found a town
i founded a town now what
why is nobody in my new town
how long until my village is built
what are the next steps after founding
entries.answer: The ground round the spot is levelled first. When the heart is level the first founder comes with the stores and puts the village board up; the rest follow a few at a time, choose trades, pitch camp and start on the well, houses and fields. You need do nothing.
steps: Watch the action bar: it says how the levelling is going.
The welcome card says what comes next. Once folk have come, use its buttons: Find the elder (it glows), The town's books, Follow the elder (a favourite), Your life in town.
A notice tells you when all the founders are there.
controls: Welcome card → Find the elder · The town's books · Follow the elder · Your life in town · Guide
tips: You can walk away: the work carries on with nobody near, and after a restart.
The first founder is the town's first elder.

entries.title: The ground is levelled for a new town
q: why is the ground being flattened
how big is the levelled area
entries.answer: A rounded square round the spot is brought to one level (hills cut, hollows filled, trees cleared, the land's own soil laid five deep) and its edge eased into the land by slopes, never cliffs. Rivers, lakes and the sea are left as they are.
tips: Nothing anybody built is touched: a column with so much as a plank or a torch is left alone, with two columns round it.
About 85 by 85 blocks for a hamlet, 99 for 25 folk, 139 for 100, 251 for 500.

entries.title: Founding Kit
q: how do i get a founding kit
how to craft a founding kit
what do i do with the founding kit
entries.answer: The Founding Kit founds a town of your own: right-click it to open the founding screen. Every new player is given one the first time they join. Craft another from 2 bread, wheat seeds, any planks and a gold nugget (shapeless).
steps: Right-click it to open the founding screen.
Choose where, how big, a name and a look; Confirm and found.

entries.title: Village Folk Spawner and the waiting board
q: what does the village folk spawner do
how do i use the folk spawner
how do i add more folk to my town
add a settler to my village
entries.answer: Placed where there's no town, the Village Folk Spawner puts up a waiting village board: right-click it to choose how many folk (2 to 500) and confirm. Placed inside a town's reach, it adds one settler. Craft it from 4 bread round a gold nugget, or 8 bread round a gold ingot.
steps: Place it on open ground: the board goes up on the edge of the future square.
Right-click the board: set How many (presets or slider; Shift for ten at a time) and read What that means.
Confirm and spawn. The ground is levelled and the folk come.
To call it off, take the board down: you get your spawner back.
controls: [Right-click] the waiting board → Confirm and spawn
tips: Right-clicked in the air away from any town, a spawner opens the easy founding screen instead.
You must stand within 24 blocks of the board to confirm.

entries.title: Village Charter
q: what does the village charter do
how do i use a charter
found a town with a charter
entries.answer: Right-click the ground with a Village Charter to found a town of seventy there (the server's default); its ground is levelled first and the folk come when the heart is level, each with a bed and four coins for the treasury. Craft it from paper, bread, wheat seeds and a gold nugget (shapeless), or the larger shaped recipe with a chest.
tips: Right-clicked in the air away from any town, it opens the founding screen, where you choose the size.
warn: Don't confuse it with a business charter: that's the fee for starting a business, not an item.

entries.title: Village Board
q: can i place a village board
entries.answer: The village board stands on the square and says what the town is doing; right-click it for the town's books. Its header has buttons such as You (your life in town) and New village. Take a town's board down and the town makes another from its stores within a minute or two.
tips: Craft one from 5 signs, 2 planks and a book to put up a board of your own anywhere.
The board lists the candidates at election time and the Wanted orders.

entries.title: Towns in the world, and vanilla villagers
q: what happened to the normal villagers
can i trade with normal villagers
entries.answer: Towns of folk appear in groups of three to five as you explore (if the server's natural villages setting is on), each levelled before its folk come. Vanilla villagers are left as they are: folk and villagers are two peoples, and a town's emerald trader walks out to trade with them.
tips: Wandering traders are untouched.
An old setting can turn villagers into folk as you meet them (off by default).

entries.title: Colonies and roads between towns
q: does my town make new towns
why did my town found another town
how are roads built between towns
entries.answer: A grown town sends out colonies, which found towns of their own, and a road is laid between mother and colony: a worn path following the land, bridges over water, lamp posts along it, and a signpost at each end. Caravans run the road every two days carrying what one town can spare to the other.
tips: Meet a caravan on the road and ask its carrier what it's doing, or to trade.
A Capital needs two colonies of its own.
